'''Jon August Wellner''' (born August 17, 1945) is an American statistician known for his contributions to the fields of statistical inference, [[empirical process theory]], and [[survival analysis]].<ref name="festschriftpreface">{{Cite book |title=From Probability to Statistics and Back: High-Dimensional Models and Processes -- A Festschrift in Honor of Jon A. Wellner |url=https://projecteuclid.org/ebooks/institute-of-mathematical-statistics-collections/from-probability-to-statistics-and-back-high-dimensional-models-and-processes-a-festschrift-in-honor-of-jon-a-wellner/toc/10.1214/12-IMSCOLL9 |doi=10.1214/12-imscoll9|isbn=9780940600836 |author1-link=Moulinath Banerjee|last1=Banerjee |first1=Moulinath |last2=Bunea |first2=Florentina |author2-link=Florentina Bunea |last3=Huang |first3=Jian |last4=Koltchinskii |first4=Vladimir |last5=Maathuis |first5=Marloes |author5-link=Marloes Maathuis |year=2013|arxiv=1808.05014|jstor=26771023 | chapter=Preface }}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Wellner was born in [[Portland, Oregon]], and grew up in various cities in the US. His father was United States Forest Service scientist [[Charles Wellner]]. He attended [[Ogden High School]] in Ogden, Utah and graduated in 1963.<ref name="festschriftbio">{{Cite book |title=From Probability to Statistics and Back: High-Dimensional Models and Processes -- A Festschrift in Honor of Jon A. Wellner |url=https://projecteuclid.org/ebooks/institute-of-mathematical-statistics-collections/from-probability-to-statistics-and-back-high-dimensional-models-and-processes-a-festschrift-in-honor-of-jon-a-wellner/toc/10.1214/12-IMSCOLL9 |doi=10.1214/12-imscoll9|isbn=9780940600836 |author1-link=Moulinath Banerjee |last1=Banerjee |first1=Moulinath |last2=Bunea |first2=Florentina |author2-link=Florentina Bunea |last3=Huang |first3=Jian |last4=Koltchinskii |first4=Vladimir |last5=Maathuis |first5=Marloes |author5-link=Marloes Maathuis |year=2013|arxiv=1808.05014|jstor=26771023 | chapter=Biography }}</ref> He went on to attend the [[University of Idaho]] in [[Moscow, Idaho]], where he earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Mathematics and Physics in 1968. After a brief stint in graduate school at [[Yale University]] in 1969–1970 and serving in the [[U.S. Army Signal Corps]] from 1969 to 1971, he returned to graduate study in statistics at the [[University of Washington]] and received his Ph.D. in 1975 with [[Galen Shorack]] as his advisor.<ref name=SS>{{Cite journal |last1=Banerjee |first1=Moulinath |author1-link=Moulinath Banerjee |last2=Samworth |authorlink2=Richard Samworth |first2=Richard J. |date=2018-11-01 |title=A Conversation with Jon Wellner |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/statistical-science/volume-33/issue-4/A-Conversation-with-Jon-Wellner/10.1214/18-STS670.full |journal=Statistical Science |volume=33 |issue=4 |doi=10.1214/18-STS670 |s2cid=88523234 |issn=0883-4237|arxiv=1808.05014 }}</ref><ref name=CV>{{Cite web |title=Biographical Sketch of Jon A. Wellner |url=https://sites.stat.washington.edu/jaw/jaw.shtvita.html |access-date=2023-04-13 |website=sites.stat.washington.edu}}</ref>

Wellner worked as an assistant professor and associate professor of statistics at the [[University of Rochester]] from 1975 to 1983, after which he moved back to the [[University of Washington]] in [[Seattle, Washington]] and became a professor of statistics. He remained at the University of Washington for the rest of his career, retiring in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jon Wellner retires after 37 years at UW {{!}} Biostatistics |url=https://www.biostat.washington.edu/news/stories/jon-wellner-retires-after-37-years-uw |first=Deb |last=Nelson |access-date=2023-04-13 |website=www.biostat.washington.edu}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Wellner was elected a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] (IMS) in 1983, a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1994, and a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] (ASA) in 2006; he became an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 2010. He was the Noether Distinguished Scholar of the ASA in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gottfried E. Noether Awards |url=https://www.amstat.org/your-career/awards/gottfried-e-noether-awards |access-date=2023-10-17 |website=Default}}</ref> He gave the Le Cam lecture of the IMS in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics {{!}} Le Cam Lecture preview: Jon A. Wellner |url=https://imstat.org/2015/04/01/le-cam-lecture-preview-jon-a-wellner/ |access-date=2023-10-17 |language=en}}</ref> He served as the executive editor of ''[[Statistical Science]]''. Wellner was the president of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics between 2016 and 2017. In 2010, he was made a [[Knight of the Order of the Netherlands Lion]].<ref name=SS /><ref name=CV />  A conference in honor of Wellner's 65th birthday was held in July of 2010.<ref name="festschriftpreface"/>
